<h1 id="fusionauth-api">FusionAuth API v1.70.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This is a FusionAuth server. Find out more at [https://fusionauth.io](https://fusionauth.io). You need to [set up an API key](https://fusionauth.io/docs/v1/tech/apis/authentication#managing-api-keys) in the FusionAuth instance you are using to test out the API calls.

Base URLs:

* <a href="http://localhost:9011">http://localhost:9011</a>

* <a href="https://sandbox.fusionauth.io">https://sandbox.fusionauth.io</a>

License: Apache2

# Authentication

* API Key (ApiKeyAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

<h1 id="fusionauth-api-default">Default</h1>

## retrieveJsonWebKeySetWithId

<a id="opIdretrieveJsonWebKeySetWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/.well-known/jwks.json \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /.well-known/jwks.json`

Returns public keys used by FusionAuth to cryptographically verify JWTs using the JSON Web Key format.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "keys": [
    {
      "alg": "ES256",
      "crv": "string",
      "d": "string",
      "dp": "string",
      "dq": "string",
      "e": "string",
      "kid": "string",
      "kty": "EC",
      "n": "string",
      "other": {
        "property1": {},
        "property2": {}
      },
      "p": "string",
      "q": "string",
      "qi": "string",
      "use": "string",
      "x": "string",
      "x5c": [
        "string"
      ],
      "x5t": "string",
      "x5t#S256": "string",
      "y": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrievejsonwebkeysetwithid-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[JWKSResponse](#schemajwksresponse)|
|default|Default|Error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## createAPIKey

<a id="opIdcreateAPIKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/api-key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "apiKey": {
      "expirationInstant": "1659380719000",
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "insertInstant": "1659380719000",
      "ipAccessControlListId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "key": "string",
      "keyManager": true,
      "lastUpdateInstant": "1659380719000",
      "metaData": {
        "attributes": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        }
      },
      "name": "string",
      "permissions": {
        "endpoints": {
          "property1": [
            null
          ],
          "property2": [
            null
          ]
        }
      },
      "retrievable": true,
      "tenantId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    },
    "sourceKeyId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /api/api-key`

Creates an API key. You can optionally specify a unique Id for the key, if not provided one will be generated. an API key can only be created with equal or lesser authority. An API key cannot create another API key unless it is granted  to that API key.  If an API key is locked to a tenant, it can only create API Keys for that same tenant.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "apiKey": {
    "expirationInstant": "1659380719000",
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "insertInstant": "1659380719000",
    "ipAccessControlListId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "key": "string",
    "keyManager": true,
    "lastUpdateInstant": "1659380719000",
    "metaData": {
      "attributes": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    },
    "name": "string",
    "permissions": {
      "endpoints": {
        "property1": [
          null
        ],
        "property2": [
          null
        ]
      }
    },
    "retrievable": true,
    "tenantId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  },
  "sourceKeyId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

|» sourceKeyId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|

> Example responses

## retrieveApplication

<a id="opIdretrieveApplication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/application \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/application`

Retrieves all the applications that are currently inactive. OR Retrieves the application for the given Id or all the applications if the Id is null.

<h3 id="retrieveapplication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|inactive|query|string|false|none|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

<h3 id="createapplication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

## searchApplicationsWithId

<a id="opIdsearchApplicationsWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/application/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "search": {
      "name": "string",
      "state": "Active",
      "tenantId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "universal": true,
      "numberOfResults": 0,
      "orderBy": "string",
      "startRow": 0
    },
    "expand": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/application/search`

Searches applications with the specified criteria and pagination.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "search": {
    "name": "string",
    "state": "Active",
    "tenantId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "universal": true,
    "numberOfResults": 0,
    "orderBy": "string",
    "startRow": 0
  },
  "expand": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="searchapplicationswithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ApplicationSearchRequest](#schemaapplicationsearchrequest)|false|none|
|» search|body|[ApplicationSearchCriteria](#schemaapplicationsearchcriteria)|false|Search criteria for Applications|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## retrieveApplicationWithId

<a id="opIdretrieveApplicationWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/application/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/application/{applicationId}`

Retrieves the application for the given Id or all the applications if the Id is null.

<h3 id="retrieveapplicationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The application Id.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

<h3 id="updateapplicationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application to update.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|reactivate|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

<h3 id="createapplicationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id to use for the application. If not provided a secure random UUID will be generated.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

## deleteApplicationWithId

<a id="opIddeleteApplicationWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/application/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/application/{applicationId}`

Hard deletes an application. This is a dangerous operation and should not be used in most circumstances. This will delete the application, any registrations for that application, metrics and reports for the application, all the roles for the application, and any other data associated with the application. This operation could take a very long time, depending on the amount of data in your database. OR Deactivates the application with the given Id.

<h3 id="deleteapplicationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hardDelete|query|string|false|none|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application to delete.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

<h3 id="patchapplicationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application to update.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## retrieveOauthConfigurationWithId

<a id="opIdretrieveOauthConfigurationWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/application/string/oauth-configuration \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/application/{applicationId}/oauth-configuration`

Retrieves the Oauth2 configuration for the application for the given Application Id.

<h3 id="retrieveoauthconfigurationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the Application to retrieve OAuth configuration.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "httpSessionMaxInactiveInterval": 0,
  "logoutURL": "string",
  "oauthConfiguration": {
    "authorizedOriginURLs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "authorizedRedirectURLs": [
      "string"
    ],
    "authorizedResourceUris": [
```

`POST /api/application/{applicationId}/role`

Creates a new role for an application. You must specify the Id of the application you are creating the role for. You can optionally specify an Id for the role inside the ApplicationRole object itself, if not provided one will be generated.

<h3 id="createapplicationrole-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application to create the role on.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

<h3 id="updateapplicationrolewithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application that the role belongs to.|
|roleId|path|string|true|The Id of the role to update.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

`POST /api/application/{applicationId}/role/{roleId}`

Creates a new role for an application. You must specify the Id of the application you are creating the role for. You can optionally specify an Id for the role inside the ApplicationRole object itself, if not provided one will be generated.

<h3 id="createapplicationrolewithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application to create the role on.|
|roleId|path|string|true|The Id of the role. If not provided a secure random UUID will be generated.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

## deleteApplicationRoleWithId

<a id="opIddeleteApplicationRoleWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/application/string/role/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /api/application/{applicationId}/role/{roleId}`

Hard deletes an application role. This is a dangerous operation and should not be used in most circumstances. This permanently removes the given role from all users that had it.

<h3 id="deleteapplicationrolewithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application that the role belongs to.|
|roleId|path|string|true|The Id of the role to delete.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

<h3 id="patchapplicationrolewithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application that the role belongs to.|
|roleId|path|string|true|The Id of the role to update.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[ApplicationRequest](#schemaapplicationrequest)|false|none|
|» application|body|[Application](#schemaapplication)|false|none|
|» role|body|[ApplicationRole](#schemaapplicationrole)|false|A role given to a user for a specific application.|
|» sourceApplicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

## refreshEntitySearchIndexWithId

<a id="opIdrefreshEntitySearchIndexWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/entity/search \
  -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`PUT /api/entity/search`

Request a refresh of the Entity search index. This API is not generally necessary and the search index will become consistent in a reasonable amount of time. There may be scenarios where you may wish to manually request an index refresh. One example may be  if you are using the Search API or Delete Tenant API immediately following a Entity Create etc, you may wish to request a refresh to  ensure the index immediately current before making a query request to the search index.

`DELETE /api/entity/type/{entityTypeId}/permission/{permissionId}`

## retrieveIdentityProviderByTypeWithId

<a id="opIdretrieveIdentityProviderByTypeWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/identity-provider \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/identity-provider`

Retrieves one or more identity provider for the given type. For types such as Google, Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn, only a single  identity provider can exist. For types such as OpenID Connect and SAMLv2 more than one identity provider can be configured so this request  may return multiple identity providers.

## retrieveIdentityProviderLookup

<a id="opIdretrieveIdentityProviderLookup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/identity-provider/lookup \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/identity-provider/lookup`

Retrieves the identity provider for the given domain and tenantId. A 200 response code indicates the domain is managed by a registered identity provider. A 404 indicates the domain is not managed. OR Retrieves any global identity providers for the given domain. A 200 response code indicates the domain is managed by a registered identity provider. A 404 indicates the domain is not managed.

<h3 id="retrieveidentityproviderlookup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|query|string|false|The domain or email address to lookup.|
|tenantId|query|string|false|If provided, the API searches for an identity provider scoped to the corresponding tenant that manages the requested domain. If no result is found, the API then searches for global identity providers.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "identityProvider": {
    "applicationIds": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "idpEndpoint": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "oauth2": {
      "authorization_endpoint": "string",
      "clientAuthenticationMethod": "none",
      "client_id": "string",
      "client_secret": "string",
      "emailClaim": "string",
      "emailVerifiedClaim": "string",
      "issuer": "string",
      "scope": "string",
      "token_endpoint": "string",
      "uniqueIdClaim": "string",
      "userinfo_endpoint": "string",
      "usernameClaim": "string"
    },
    "tenantId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "type": "Apple"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieveidentityproviderlookup-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[LookupResponse](#schemalookupresponse)|
|default|Default|Error|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

<a id="opIddeleteJwtRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/jwt/refresh \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "applicationId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "token": "string",
    "userId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "eventInfo": {
      "data": {
        "property1": {},
        "property2": {}
      },
      "deviceDescription": "string",
      "deviceName": "string",
      "deviceType": "string",
      "ipAddress": "string",
      "location": {
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "latitude": 0,
        "longitude": 0,
        "region": "string",
        "zipcode": "string",
        "displayString": "string"
      },
      "os": "string",
      "userAgent": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`DELETE /api/jwt/refresh`

Revokes refresh tokens using the information in the JSON body. The handling for this method is the same as the revokeRefreshToken method and is based on the information you provide in the RefreshDeleteRequest object. See that method for additional information. OR Revoke all refresh tokens that belong to a user by user Id for a specific application by applicationId. OR Revoke all refresh tokens that belong to a user by user Id. OR Revoke all refresh tokens that belong to an application by applicationId. OR Revokes a single refresh token by using the actual refresh token value. This refresh token value is sensitive, so  be careful with this API request. OR Revokes refresh tokens.  Usage examples:   - Delete a single refresh token, pass in only the token.       revokeRefreshToken(token)    - Delete all refresh tokens for a user, pass in only the userId.       revokeRefreshToken(null, userId)    - Delete all refresh tokens for a user for a specific application, pass in both the userId and the applicationId.       revokeRefreshToken(null, userId, applicationId)    - Delete all refresh tokens for an application       revokeRefreshToken(null, null, applicationId)  Note: <code>null</code> may be handled differently depending upon the programming language.  See also: (method names may vary by language... but you'll figure it out)   - revokeRefreshTokenById  - revokeRefreshTokenByToken  - revokeRefreshTokensByUserId  - revokeRefreshTokensByApplicationId  - revokeRefreshTokensByUserIdForApplication

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "applicationId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "token": "string",
  "userId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "eventInfo": {
    "data": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "deviceDescription": "string",
    "deviceName": "string",
    "deviceType": "string",
    "ipAddress": "string",
    "location": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "latitude": 0,
      "longitude": 0,
      "region": "string",
      "zipcode": "string",
      "displayString": "string"
    },
    "os": "string",
    "userAgent": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="deletejwtrefresh-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|applicationId|query|string|false|The unique Id of the application that you want to delete refresh tokens for.|

## validateJWTWithId

<a id="opIdvalidateJWTWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/jwt/validate \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/jwt/validate`

Validates the provided JWT (encoded JWT string) to ensure the token is valid. A valid access token is properly signed and not expired. <p> This API may be used to verify the JWT as well as decode the encoded JWT into human readable identity claims.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "jwt": {
    "aud": {},
    "exp": "1659380719000",
    "iat": "1659380719000",
    "iss": "string",
    "nbf": "1659380719000",
    "otherClaims": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "sub": "string",
    "jti": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="validatejwtwithid-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[ValidateResponse](#schemavalidateresponse)|
|default|Default|Error|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BearerAuth

## vendJWTWithId

<a id="opIdvendJWTWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/jwt/vend \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "claims": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "keyId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "timeToLiveInSeconds": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/jwt/vend`

It's a JWT vending machine!  Issue a new access token (JWT) with the provided claims in the request. This JWT is not scoped to a tenant or user, it is a free form  token that will contain what claims you provide. <p> The iat, exp and jti claims will be added by FusionAuth, all other claims must be provided by the caller.  If a TTL is not provided in the request, the TTL will be retrieved from the default Tenant or the Tenant specified on the request either  by way of the X-FusionAuth-TenantId request header, or a tenant scoped API key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "claims": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "keyId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "timeToLiveInSeconds": 0
}
```

<h3 id="vendjwtwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[JWTVendRequest](#schemajwtvendrequest)|false|none|
|» claims|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» keyId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» timeToLiveInSeconds|body|integer|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "fieldErrors": {
    "property1": [
      {
        "code": "string",
        "data": {
          "property1": {},
          "property2": {}
        },
        "message": "string"
      }
    ],
    "property2": [
      {
        "code": "string",
        "data": {
          "property1": {},
          "property2": {}
        },
        "message": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "generalErrors": [
    {
      "code": "string",
      "data": {
        "property1": {},
        "property2": {}
      },
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|default|Default|Error|[Errors](#schemaerrors)|

`PUT /api/login`

Sends a ping to FusionAuth indicating that the user was automatically logged into an application. When using FusionAuth's SSO or your own, you should call this if the user is already logged in centrally, but accesses an application where they no longer have a session. This helps correctly track login counts, times and helps with reporting.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "userId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "applicationId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "botDetectionScore": 0,
  "ipAddress": "string",
  "metaData": {
    "data": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "device": {
      "description": "string",
      "lastAccessedAddress": "string",
      "lastAccessedInstant": "1659380719000",
      "name": "string",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "resources": [
      "string"
    ],
    "scopes": [
      null
    ]
  },
  "newDevice": true,
  "noJWT": true
}
```

<h3 id="loginpingwithrequestwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[LoginPingRequest](#schemaloginpingrequest)|false|none|
|» userId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» applicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» botDetectionScore|body|number(double)|false|none|
|» ipAddress|body|string|false|none|
|» metaData|body|[MetaData](#schemametadata)|false|none|
|» newDevice|body|boolean|false|none|
|» noJWT|body|boolean|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "actions": [
```

`POST /api/login`

Authenticates a user to FusionAuth.   This API optionally requires an API key. See <code>Application.loginConfiguration.requireAuthentication</code>.

```json
}
```

## loginPingWithId

<a id="opIdloginPingWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/login/string/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`PUT /api/login/{userId}/{applicationId}`

Sends a ping to FusionAuth indicating that the user was automatically logged into an application. When using FusionAuth's SSO or your own, you should call this if the user is already logged in centrally, but accesses an application where they no longer have a session. This helps correctly track login counts, times and helps with reporting.

<h3 id="loginpingwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ipAddress|query|string|false|The IP address of the end-user that is logging in. If a null value is provided the IP address will be that of the client or last proxy that sent the request.|
|userId|path|string|true|The Id of the user that was logged in.|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application that they logged into.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

`POST /api/logout`

The Logout API is intended to be used to remove the refresh token and access token cookies if they exist on the client and revoke the refresh token stored. This API takes the refresh token in the JSON body. OR The Logout API is intended to be used to remove the refresh token and access token cookies if they exist on the client and revoke the refresh token stored. This API does nothing if the request does not contain an access token or refresh token cookies.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "global": true,
  "refreshToken": "string",
  "eventInfo": {
    "data": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "deviceDescription": "string",
    "deviceName": "string",
    "deviceType": "string",
    "ipAddress": "string",
    "location": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "latitude": 0,
      "longitude": 0,
      "region": "string",
      "zipcode": "string",
      "displayString": "string"
    },
    "os": "string",
    "userAgent": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="createlogout-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|global|query|string|false|When this value is set to true all the refresh tokens issued to the owner of the provided token will be revoked.|
|refreshToken|query|string|false|The refresh_token as a request parameter instead of coming in via a cookie. If provided this takes precedence over the cookie.|
|body|body|[LogoutRequest](#schemalogoutrequest)|false|none|
|» global|body|boolean|false|none|
|» refreshToken|body|string|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

`GET /api/report/registration`

Retrieves the registration report between the two instants. If you specify an application Id, it will only return the registration counts for that application.

<h3 id="retrieveregistrationreportwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|query|string|false|The application Id.|
|start|query|string|false|The start instant as UTC milliseconds since Epoch.|
|end|query|string|false|The end instant as UTC milliseconds since Epoch.|

`POST /api/system/audit-log`

Creates an audit log with the message and user name (usually an email). Audit logs should be written anytime you make changes to the FusionAuth database. When using the FusionAuth App web interface, any changes are automatically written to the audit log. However, if you are accessing the API, you must write the audit logs yourself.

<h3 id="createtenant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[TenantRequest](#schematenantrequest)|false|none|
|» sourceTenantId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» tenant|body|[Tenant](#schematenant)|false|none|
|» webhookIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

## retrieveTenantWithId

<a id="opIdretrieveTenantWithId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/tenant/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/tenant/{tenantId}`

Retrieves the tenant for the given Id.

<h3 id="retrievetenantwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenantId|path|string|true|The Id of the tenant.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|

<h3 id="updatetenantwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenantId|path|string|true|The Id of the tenant to update.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[TenantRequest](#schematenantrequest)|false|none|
|» sourceTenantId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» tenant|body|[Tenant](#schematenant)|false|none|
|» webhookIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

<h3 id="createtenantwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenantId|path|string|true|The Id for the tenant. If not provided a secure random UUID will be generated.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[TenantRequest](#schematenantrequest)|false|none|
|» sourceTenantId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» tenant|body|[Tenant](#schematenant)|false|none|
|» webhookIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

`DELETE /api/tenant/{tenantId}`

Deletes the tenant based on the given request (sent to the API as JSON). This permanently deletes all information, metrics, reports and data associated with the tenant and everything under the tenant (applications, users, etc). OR Deletes the tenant for the given Id asynchronously. This method is helpful if you do not want to wait for the delete operation to complete. OR Deletes the tenant based on the given Id on the URL. This permanently deletes all information, metrics, reports and data associated with the tenant and everything under the tenant (applications, users, etc).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "async": true,
  "eventInfo": {
    "data": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "deviceDescription": "string",
    "deviceName": "string",
    "deviceType": "string",
    "ipAddress": "string",
    "location": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "latitude": 0,
      "longitude": 0,
      "region": "string",
      "zipcode": "string",
      "displayString": "string"
    },
    "os": "string",
    "userAgent": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="deletetenantwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenantId|path|string|true|The Id of the tenant to delete.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|async|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|[TenantDeleteRequest](#schematenantdeleterequest)|false|none|
|» async|body|boolean|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

<h3 id="patchtenantwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenantId|path|string|true|The Id of the tenant to update.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[TenantRequest](#schematenantrequest)|false|none|
|» sourceTenantId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» tenant|body|[Tenant](#schematenant)|false|none|
|» webhookIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

`GET /api/two-factor/secret`

Generate a Two Factor secret that can be used to enable Two Factor authentication for a User. The response will contain both the secret and a Base32 encoded form of the secret which can be shown to a User when using a 2 Step Authentication application such as Google Authenticator.

`POST /api/two-factor/start`

Start a Two-Factor login request by generating a two-factor identifier. This code can then be sent to the Two Factor Send  API (/api/two-factor/send)in order to send a one-time use code to a user. You can also use one-time use code returned  to send the code out-of-band. The Two-Factor login is completed by making a request to the Two-Factor Login  API (/api/two-factor/login). with the two-factor identifier and the one-time use code.  This API is intended to allow you to begin a Two-Factor login outside a normal login that originated from the Login API (/api/login).

## retrieveUser

<a id="opIdretrieveUser"></a>

`GET /api/user`

Retrieves the user by a verificationId. The intended use of this API is to retrieve a user after the forgot password workflow has been initiated and you may not know the user's email or username. OR Retrieves the user for the given username. OR Retrieves the user for the loginId, using specific loginIdTypes. OR Retrieves the user for the loginId. The loginId can be either the username or the email. OR Retrieves the user for the given email. OR Retrieves the user by a change password Id. The intended use of this API is to retrieve a user after the forgot password workflow has been initiated and you may not know the user's email or username.

|username|query|string|false|The username of the user.|
|loginId|query|string|false|The email or username of the user.|
|loginIdTypes|query|[string]|false|The identity types that FusionAuth will compare the loginId to.|
|email|query|string|false|The email of the user.|

<h3 id="createuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[UserRequest](#schemauserrequest)|false|none|
|» applicationId|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» currentPassword|body|string|false|none|
|» disableDomainBlock|body|boolean|false|none|
|» passwordFieldType|body|[PasswordType](#schemapasswordtype)|false|Indicates whether a password is plaintext or hashed|
|» sendSetPasswordEmail|body|boolean|false|none|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|body|[SendSetPasswordIdentityType](#schemasendsetpasswordidentitytype)|false|Used to indicate which identity type a password "request" might go to. It could be  used for send set passwords or send password resets.|
|» skipVerification|body|boolean|false|none|
|» user|body|[User](#schemauser)|false|The public, global view of a User. This object contains all global information about the user including birthdate, registration information  preferred languages, global attributes, etc.|
|» verificationIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» passwordFieldType|PLAINTEXT|
|» passwordFieldType|HASHED|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|email|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|phone|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|doNotSend|

## retrieveUserAction

<a id="opIdretrieveUserAction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/user-action \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/user-action`

Retrieves the user action for the given Id. If you pass in null for the Id, this will return all the user actions. OR Retrieves all the user actions that are currently inactive.

<h3 id="retrieveuseraction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|inactive|query|string|false|none|

## retrieveUserActioning

<a id="opIdretrieveUserActioning"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/user/action \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/user/action`

Retrieves all the actions for the user with the given Id that are currently inactive. An inactive action means one that is time based and has been canceled or has expired, or is not time based. OR Retrieves all the actions for the user with the given Id that are currently active. An active action means one that is time based and has not been canceled, and has not ended. OR Retrieves all the actions for the user with the given Id that are currently preventing the User from logging in. OR Retrieves all the actions for the user with the given Id. This will return all time based actions that are active, and inactive as well as non-time based actions.

<h3 id="retrieveuseractioning-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|query|string|false|The Id of the user to fetch the actions for.|
|active|query|string|false|none|
|preventingLogin|query|string|false|none|

## deleteUserBulk

<a id="opIddeleteUserBulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/user/bulk \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "dryRun": true,
    "hardDelete": true,
    "limit": 0,
    "query": "string",
    "queryString": "string",
    "userIds": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"

        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "latitude": 0,
        "longitude": 0,
        "region": "string",
        "zipcode": "string",
        "displayString": "string"
      },
      "os": "string",
      "userAgent": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`DELETE /api/user/bulk`

Deletes the users with the given Ids, or users matching the provided JSON query or queryString. The order of preference is Ids, query and then queryString, it is recommended to only provide one of the three for the request.  This method can be used to deactivate or permanently delete (hard-delete) users based upon the hardDelete boolean in the request body. Using the dryRun parameter you may also request the result of the action without actually deleting or deactivating any users. OR Deactivates the users with the given Ids.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dryRun": true,
  "hardDelete": true,
  "limit": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "queryString": "string",
  "userIds": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "eventInfo": {
    "data": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "deviceDescription": "string",
    "deviceName": "string",
    "deviceType": "string",
    "ipAddress": "string",
    "location": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "latitude": 0,
      "longitude": 0,
      "region": "string",
      "zipcode": "string",
      "displayString": "string"
    },
    "os": "string",
    "userAgent": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="deleteuserbulk-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|query|string|false|The ids of the users to deactivate.|
|dryRun|query|string|false|none|
|hardDelete|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|[UserDeleteRequest](#schemauserdeleterequest)|false|none|

## retrieveUserChangePassword

<a id="opIdretrieveUserChangePassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/api/user/change-password \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/user/change-password`

Check to see if the user must obtain a Trust Request Id in order to complete a change password request. When a user has enabled Two-Factor authentication, before you are allowed to use the Change Password API to change your password, you must obtain a Trust Request Id by completing a Two-Factor Step-Up authentication.  An HTTP status code of 400 with a general error code of [TrustTokenRequired] indicates that a Trust Token is required to make a POST request to this API. OR Check to see if the user must obtain a Trust Request Id in order to complete a change password request. When a user has enabled Two-Factor authentication, before you are allowed to use the Change Password API to change your password, you must obtain a Trust Request Id by completing a Two-Factor Step-Up authentication.  An HTTP status code of 400 with a general error code of [TrustTokenRequired] indicates that a Trust Token is required to make a POST request to this API. OR Check to see if the user must obtain a Trust Request Id in order to complete a change password request. When a user has enabled Two-Factor authentication, before you are allowed to use the Change Password API to change your password, you must obtain a Trust Request Id by completing a Two-Factor Step-Up authentication.  An HTTP status code of 400 with a general error code of [TrustTokenRequired] indicates that a Trust Token is required to make a POST request to this API. OR Check to see if the user must obtain a Trust Request Id in order to complete a change password request. When a user has enabled Two-Factor authentication, before you are allowed to use the Change Password API to change your password, you must obtain a Trust Request Id by completing a Two-Factor Step-Up authentication.  An HTTP status code of 400 with a general error code of [TrustTokenRequired] indicates that a Trust Token is required to make a POST request to this API. OR Check to see if the user must obtain a Trust Token Id in order to complete a change password request. When a user has enabled Two-Factor authentication, before you are allowed to use the Change Password API to change your password, you must obtain a Trust Token by completing a Two-Factor Step-Up authentication.  An HTTP status code of 400 with a general error code of [TrustTokenRequired] indicates that a Trust Token is required to make a POST request to this API. OR Check to see if the user must obtain a Trust Token Id in order to complete a change password request. When a user has enabled Two-Factor authentication, before you are allowed to use the Change Password API to change your password, you must obtain a Trust Token by completing a Two-Factor Step-Up authentication.  An HTTP status code of 400 with a general error code of [TrustTokenRequired] indicates that a Trust Token is required to make a POST request to this API.

`POST /api/user/change-password`

Changes a user's password using their access token (JWT) instead of the changePasswordId A common use case for this method will be if you want to allow the user to change their own password.  Remember to send refreshToken in the request body if you want to get a new refresh token when login using the returned oneTimePassword. OR Changes a user's password using their identity (loginId and password). Using a loginId instead of the changePasswordId bypasses the email verification and allows a password to be changed directly without first calling the #forgotPassword method.

`POST /api/user/registration`

Registers a user for an application. If you provide the User and the UserRegistration object on this request, it will create the user as well as register them for the application. This is called a Full Registration. However, if you only provide the UserRegistration object, then the user must already exist and they will be registered for the application. The user Id can also be provided and it will either be used to look up an existing user or it will be used for the newly created User.

<h3 id="updateregistrationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The Id of the user whose registration is going to be updated.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[RegistrationRequest](#schemaregistrationrequest)|false|none|
|» disableDomainBlock|body|boolean|false|none|
|» generateAuthenticationToken|body|boolean|false|none|
|» registration|body|[UserRegistration](#schemauserregistration)|false|User registration information for a single application.|
|» sendSetPasswordEmail|body|boolean|false|none|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|body|[SendSetPasswordIdentityType](#schemasendsetpasswordidentitytype)|false|Used to indicate which identity type a password "request" might go to. It could be  used for send set passwords or send password resets.|
|» skipRegistrationVerification|body|boolean|false|none|
|» skipVerification|body|boolean|false|none|
|» user|body|[User](#schemauser)|false|The public, global view of a User. This object contains all global information about the user including birthdate, registration information  preferred languages, global attributes, etc.|
|» verificationIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|email|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|phone|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|doNotSend|

`POST /api/user/registration/{userId}`

Registers a user for an application. If you provide the User and the UserRegistration object on this request, it will create the user as well as register them for the application. This is called a Full Registration. However, if you only provide the UserRegistration object, then the user must already exist and they will be registered for the application. The user Id can also be provided and it will either be used to look up an existing user or it will be used for the newly created User.

<h3 id="registerwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The Id of the user being registered for the application and optionally created.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[RegistrationRequest](#schemaregistrationrequest)|false|none|
|» disableDomainBlock|body|boolean|false|none|
|» generateAuthenticationToken|body|boolean|false|none|
|» registration|body|[UserRegistration](#schemauserregistration)|false|User registration information for a single application.|
|» sendSetPasswordEmail|body|boolean|false|none|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|body|[SendSetPasswordIdentityType](#schemasendsetpasswordidentitytype)|false|Used to indicate which identity type a password "request" might go to. It could be  used for send set passwords or send password resets.|
|» skipRegistrationVerification|body|boolean|false|none|
|» skipVerification|body|boolean|false|none|
|» user|body|[User](#schemauser)|false|The public, global view of a User. This object contains all global information about the user including birthdate, registration information  preferred languages, global attributes, etc.|
|» verificationIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|email|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|phone|
|» sendSetPasswordIdentityType|doNotSend|

`DELETE /api/user/registration/{userId}/{applicationId}`

Deletes the user registration for the given user and application along with the given JSON body that contains the event information. OR Deletes the user registration for the given user and application.

```json
}
```

<h3 id="deleteuserregistrationwithid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The Id of the user whose registration is being deleted.|
|applicationId|path|string|true|The Id of the application to remove the registration for.|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|body|body|[RegistrationDeleteRequest](#schemaregistrationdeleterequest)|false|none|

## refreshUserSearchIndexWithId

```bash

  -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`PUT /api/user/search`

Request a refresh of the User search index. This API is not generally necessary and the search index will become consistent in a reasonable amount of time. There may be scenarios where you may wish to manually request an index refresh. One example may be  if you are using the Search API or Delete Tenant API immediately following a User Create etc, you may wish to request a refresh to  ensure the index immediately current before making a query request to the search index.

`POST /api/user/verify-email`

Administratively verify a user's email address. Use this method to bypass email verification for the user.  The request body will contain the userId to be verified. An API key is required when sending the userId in the request body. OR Confirms a user's email address.   The request body will contain the verificationId. You may also be required to send a one-time use code based upon your configuration. When  the tenant is configured to gate a user until their email address is verified, this procedures requires two values instead of one.  The verificationId is a high entropy value and the one-time use code is a low entropy value that is easily entered in a user interactive form. The  two values together are able to confirm a user's email address and mark the user's email address as verified.

`DELETE /api/user/{userId}`

Deletes the user based on the given request (sent to the API as JSON). This permanently deletes all information, metrics, reports and data associated with the user. OR Deletes the user for the given Id. This permanently deletes all information, metrics, reports and data associated with the user. OR Deactivates the user with the given Id.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "hardDelete": true,
  "eventInfo": {
    "data": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "deviceDescription": "string",
    "deviceName": "string",
    "deviceType": "string",
    "ipAddress": "string",
    "location": {
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "latitude": 0,
      "longitude": 0,
      "region": "string",
      "zipcode": "string",
      "displayString": "string"
    },
    "os": "string",
    "userAgent": "string"
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The Id of the user to delete (required).|
|X-FusionAuth-TenantId|header|string(UUID)|false|The unique Id of the tenant used to scope this API request. Only required when there is more than one tenant and the API key is not tenant-scoped.|
|hardDelete|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|[UserDeleteSingleRequest](#schemauserdeletesinglerequest)|false|none|
|» hardDelete|body|boolean|false|none|
|» eventInfo|body|[EventInfo](#schemaeventinfo)|false|Information about a user event (login, register, etc) that helps identify the source of the event (location, device type, OS, etc).|

## createToken

<a id="opIdcreateToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://sandbox.fusionauth.io/oauth2/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d 'username=string&password=string&client_id=string&client_secret=string&grant_type=string&scope=string&user_code=string'
```

`POST /oauth2/token`

Exchange User Credentials for a Token. If you will be using the Resource Owner Password Credential Grant, you will make a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the user’s email and password for an access token. OR Exchange User Credentials for a Token. If you will be using the Resource Owner Password Credential Grant, you will make a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the user’s email and password for an access token. OR Exchange a Refresh Token for an Access Token. If you will be using the Refresh Token Grant, you will make a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the user’s refresh token for an access token. OR Exchange a Refresh Token for an Access Token. If you will be using the Refresh Token Grant, you will make a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the user’s refresh token for an access token. OR Exchanges an OAuth authorization code for an access token. Makes a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the authorization code returned from the Authorize endpoint for an access token. OR Exchanges an OAuth authorization code and code_verifier for an access token. Makes a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the authorization code returned from the Authorize endpoint and a code_verifier for an access token. OR Exchanges an OAuth authorization code and code_verifier for an access token. Makes a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the authorization code returned from the Authorize endpoint and a code_verifier for an access token. OR Exchanges an OAuth authorization code for an access token. Makes a request to the Token endpoint to exchange the authorization code returned from the Authorize endpoint for an access token. OR Make a Client Credentials grant request to obtain an access token. OR Make a Client Credentials grant request to obtain an access token.

> Body parameter

```yaml
username: string
password: string
client_id: string
client_secret: string
grant_type: string
scope: string
user_code: string
```

<h3 id="createtoken-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» username|body|string|false|The login identifier of the user. The login identifier can be either the email or the username.|
|» password|body|string|false|The user’s password.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The unique client identifier. The client Id is the Id of the FusionAuth Application in which you are attempting to authenticate. This parameter is optional when the Authorization header is provided. This parameter is optional when Basic Authorization is used to authenticate this request.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret. This value may optionally be provided in the request body instead of the Authorization header.|
|» grant_type|body|string|false|The grant type to be used. This value must be set to password|
|» scope|body|string|false|This parameter is optional and if omitted, the same scope requested during the authorization request will be used. If provided the scopes must match those requested during the initial authorization request.|
|» user_code|body|string|false|The end-user verification code. This code is required if using this endpoint to approve the Device Authorization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "expires_in": 0,
  "id_token": "string",
  "issued_token_type": "string",
  "refresh_token": "string",
  "refresh_token_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "scope": "string",
  "access_token": "string",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "userId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "change_password_id": "string",
  "error_description": "string",
  "error": "invalid_request",
  "error_uri": "string",
  "two_factor_methods": [
    {
      "authenticator": {
        "algorithm": "HmacSHA1",

      },

      "name": "string",
      "secret": "string"
    }
  ],
```

Used by the Relying Party to specify their requirements for authenticator attributes. Fields use the deprecated "resident key" terminology to refer  to client-side discoverable credentials to maintain backwards compatibility with WebAuthn Level 1.

|requireResidentKey|boolean|false|none|none|
|residentKey|[ResidentKeyRequirement](#schemaresidentkeyrequirement)|false|none|Describes the Relying Party's requirements for <a href="https:www.w3.orgTRwebauthn-2#client-side-discoverable-credential">client-side  discoverable credentials<a> (formerly known as "resident keys")|
|userVerification|[UserVerificationRequirement](#schemauserverificationrequirement)|false|none|Used to express whether the Relying Party requires <a href="https:www.w3.orgTRwebauthn-2#user-verification">user verification<a> for the  current operation.|

<a id="tocsfips"></a>

```json
{}
```

Determines if FusionAuth is in FIPS mode based on the system property <code>fusionauth.fips.enabled<code>. This can only be enabled once and  should be enabled when the VM starts or as close to that point as possible.  <p>  Once this has been enabled, it cannot be disabled.  <p>  This also provides some helpers for FIPS things such as password length requirements.

JSON Web Token (JWT) as defined by RFC 7519.  <pre>  From RFC 7519 Section 1. Introduction:     The suggested pronunciation of JWT is the same as the English word "jot".  <pre>  The JWT is not Thread-Safe and should not be re-used.

|iat|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|false|none|The number of milliseconds since the unix epoch: January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. This value is always in UTC.|
|iss|string|false|none|none|
|nbf|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|false|none|The number of milliseconds since the unix epoch: January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. This value is always in UTC.|

|sub|string|false|none|none|
|jti|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ManagedFields">ManagedFields</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamanagedfields"></a>
<a id="schema_ManagedFields"></a>
<a id="tocSmanagedfields"></a>
<a id="tocsmanagedfields"></a>

```json
{}
```

Contains the "managed"{@link FormField} keys. For these keys, FusionAuth controls the  field's control and data type.  <p>  The data type is always enforced, on both create and update.  The control is only defaulted  when omitted on create, and is otherwise left as submitted - it is not validated against  the managed definition. Once created, a mismatched control can only be fixed by deleting  and recreating the field, since updates always keep the field's existing control.  <p>  Internal Note: These fields are also declared in SQL in order to bootstrap the system. These need to stay in sync.  Any changes to these fields needs to also be reflected in mysql.sql and postgresql.sql

An audit record for a single token exchange attempt. Exactly one of these is written for every attempt, whether it succeeded or failed,  so this is the authoritative record of who exchanged what for what.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|actChain|string|false|none|none|
|delegationSemantics|[TokenExchangeDelegationSemantics](#schematokenexchangedelegationsemantics)|false|none|The delegation semantics applied to the issued token. These are RFC 8693 terms.  FusionAuth does not support token exchange impersonation.|
|eventId|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|exchangerClientId|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|grantedAudience|string|false|none|none|
|grantedScope|string|false|none|none|
|insertInstant|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|false|none|The number of milliseconds since the unix epoch: January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. This value is always in UTC.|
|intent|string|false|none|none|
|issuedTokenJti|string|false|none|none|
|outcome|[TokenExchangeOutcome](#schematokenexchangeoutcome)|false|none|The terminal outcome of a token exchange attempt. Every failure stage gets a distinct value so a denial can be attributed to the stage  that rejected it.|
|policyDecision|[TokenExchangePolicyDecision](#schematokenexchangepolicydecision)|false|none|The decision returned by the policy engine.|
|policyDecisionDurationMs|integer|false|none|none|
|policyEngine|[TokenExchangePolicyEngine](#schematokenexchangepolicyengine)|false|none|The policy engine used to authorize an RFC 8693 token exchange request.|
|requestedAudience|string|false|none|none|
|subjectTokenIss|string|false|none|none|
|subjectTokenJti|string|false|none|none|
|subjectTokenSub|string|false|none|none|
|subjectTokenType|string|false|none|none|
|subjectTokenValidationStatus|[SubjectTokenValidationStatus](#schemasubjecttokenvalidationstatus)|false|none|How much confidence we have in the validation of the subject token that was presented. These values are specified by the ARC and are  stored by name, so they may not be renamed without a migration.|
|tenantId|string(uuid)|false|none|none|

```json
}
```

The system configuration for token exchange audit log data.  <p>  Deleting these entries is mandatory, so this configuration intentionally has no enabled flag. Token exchange volume can be high enough  that retaining entries indefinitely would grow the database without bound. Longer retention is served by ingesting the token exchange  webhooks into external storage.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|numberOfDaysToRetain|integer|false|none|none|
